questions.question: What are NgRx Effects? How do they handle async side effects?
questions.title: NgRx Effects — Handling Async Side Effects Cleanly
questions.direct_answer:
What are NgRx Effects? How do they handle async side effects?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** createEffect for side effects; listens to actions, performs async work via RxJS operators, dispatches success/failure actions.

**Classic weak answer:** Putting side effects inside reducers — reducers must be pure; effects are the right home.

**Senior finish:** Show a loadUsers effect using switchMap → HTTP → map to success action + catchError → failure action.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **NgRx Effects — Handling Async Side Effects Cleanly** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are NgRx Effects? How do they handle async side effects?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **createEffect for side effects; listens to actions, performs async work via RxJS operators, dispatches success/failure actions**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Putting side effects inside reducers — reducers must be pure; effects are the right home**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a loadUsers effect using switchMap → HTTP → map to success action + catchError → failure action**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** createEffect for side effects; listens to actions, performs async work via RxJS operators, dispatches success/failure actions
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **putting side effects inside reducers — reducers must be pure; effects are the right home** and what you do instead.

sections.content:

- **Mechanism:** createEffect for side effects; listens to actions, performs async work via RxJS operators, dispatches success/failure actions
- **Pitfall:** Putting side effects inside reducers — reducers must be pure; effects are the right home
- **Differentiator:** Show a loadUsers effect using switchMap → HTTP → map to success action + catchError → failure action
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **createEffect for side effects; listens to actions, performs async work via RxJS operators, dispatches success/failure actions** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Putting side effects inside reducers — reducers must be pure; effects are the right home** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Show a loadUsers effect using switchMap → HTTP → map to success action + catchError → failure action**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: How do NgRx selectors work? Why are they memoized?
questions.title: NgRx Selectors — createSelector Memoization Explained
questions.direct_answer:
How do NgRx selectors work? Why are they memoized?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** createSelector combines selectors; reselect-style memoization prevents recomputation unless inputs change; combine with store.select.

**Classic weak answer:** Not memoizing selectors — template re-computes derived data on every change-detection cycle.

**Senior finish:** Show a featureSelector → property selectors → combined createSelector with OnPush component.

interviewer_intent.testing: createSelector combines selectors; reselect-style memoization prevents recomputation unless inputs change; combine with store.select
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not memoizing selectors — template re-computes derived data on every change-detection cycle
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show a featureSelector → property selectors → combined createSelector with OnPush component
